title: Adaptive SLA-encoded prioritizer and evidence-tiering playbook for enterprise security asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Enterprise prospects frequently submit complex security questionnaires (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA/vendor RFIs). Current intake routes produce uneven prioritization, unclear SLA commitments, and repeated evidence requests. Scope: Create a decision-scaffold and encoded SLA policy that converts incoming security asks into: (1) a priority score, (2) an evidence-tier assignment (bundle A/B/C), (3) automatic SLA expectations to surface to sales/CS, and (4) stakeholder routing (legal, infra, privacy, PM). Goals: reduce time-to-response for high-value deals, lower repetitive evidence assembly work by 40%, make SLA commitments auditable, and provide a small API/console view for sales to see expected delivery dates and outstanding dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Priority scoring model implemented and documented with explanation of weights
Evidence tiers defined (A/B/C) with explicit templates and ownership
SLA encoder translates priority to target response times and is surfaced in the customer portal and internal dashboard
Routing rules created that map question types to primary/secondary owners (legal, privacy, infra, PM)
Playbook published in Confluence with 2 example flows and 3 canned response templates
Pilot run with 3 active enterprise customers and measured reduction in evidence turnaround time
tasks: Workshop with sales/legal/privacy to finalize priority factors
Design evidence tier templates and link to existing Confluence evidence library
Define SLA targets (P0..P3) and map to priority scores
Implement lightweight scoring engine (serverless) and webhook to Stitch into helpdesk/Ticketing
Console UI: read-only card showing priority, SLA ETA, evidence package link
Create rollout plan and training runbook for Sales and CS
